Nineteen comments

Mickey Callaghan’s Fancy

At first, I heard this tune played as “P. J. Haye’s” in Calico’s “Celanova Square,” but later I found P. J. himself playing in Mary MacNamara’s album.

↳ Posted by slainte on June 16th, 2002.

Lovely tune. I learnt it from the Sliabh Notes recording “Gleantan” , in the key of A. It’s also on Breathnach #1 on the key of D.
I decided to tranpose it to G in order to fit it into a set between the Air “Kitty Tyrell” and the reel “Touch me if you dare”, both in G.

A variation can be done in second part’s last round, changing Bd|e2e (I actually play Bd|e3) by Gfe3

As my setting is slightly different from this one, I include it here. Enjoy.

Mickey Callaghan’s Fancy, X:6

We play this setting at my local session. The leader of the session has at times referred to it as ‘Micky O Calahan’s’ and ‘Micky O Calahan’s Fancy’ and ‘Micky O Sullivan’s’. Most often he calls it the later, though I cannot believe it, for it is so similar to Micky O Calahan’s Fancy, just in a different Key.

↳ Posted by Noah Cockett on September 6th, 2019.

Re: Mickey Callaghan’s Fancy

Its simplicity (no rolls, easily memorised) and the fact it can be played in both the keys of G and D’ make this tune an ideal beginners reel as well as a hornpipe.
